title: Article 133 — Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in regard to civil matters

content.overview: Article 133 provides for appeal to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court if the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance and that in the opinion of the High Court the said question needs to be decided by the Supreme Court. Parliament may by law enlarge the appellate jurisdiction. No appeal lies from a single Judge of a High Court unless Parliament by law otherwise provides.
content.glance: Civil appeal to SC: HC certificate under Art 134A — substantial question of law of general importance that needs SC decision. No appeal from single Judge unless Parliament provides.
content.study:
Article 133 civil appeals:
- From judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court.
- Certificate under Art 134A: substantial question of law of general importance + HC opinion that it needs to be decided by the SC.
- Parliament may enlarge appellate jurisdiction by law.
- No appeal from a single Judge of a High Court unless Parliament by law provides otherwise.

Examination: civil only; dual certificate criteria; single-Judge bar; parliamentary enlargement power.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Civil proceeding of a High Court.
2. Art 134A certificate: substantial question of law of general importance that needs SC decision.
3. Parliament may enlarge jurisdiction by law.
4. No appeal from single Judge unless Parliament provides.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When does a civil appeal lie to the Supreme Court under Article 133?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 133, an appeal lies to the Supreme Court from any judgment, decree or final order in a civil proceeding of a High Court if the High Court certifies under Article 134A that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance and that in the opinion of the High Court the question needs to be decided by the Supreme Court. No appeal lies from the judgment of a single Judge of a High Court unless Parliament by law otherwise provides.

examTips: Civil; substantial question of general importance; needs SC decision; single-Judge bar.

keyTakeaways: Art 133: civil appellate jurisdiction on certified substantial questions of general importance.
